experimental_method: Automated isochoric apparatus (spherical vessel of mercury-calibrated volume in an air thermostat): CH4 charged at about 323 K (mass from the Setzmann-Wagner EoS), a weighed mass of liquid water injected by a calibrated screw injector, then (p, T) recorded along a quasi-isochore through the two-phase and single-phase gas regions; dew points from the break in the (p, T) curve.
uncertainties_stated: T: PRT calibrated on ITS-90 by NPL, better than 0.01 K. p: quartz transducer 0.02 %. rho: '+/-0.8 per cent' for the lowest water content and '+/-0.14 per cent' for the highest (text p. 448); the abstract gives '+/-0.0008 rho' (0.08 %) and '+/-0.0014 rho'. Dew points: dTd, dpd, drho_d listed per row in Table 2 (Td generally better than 1 K).
quality_remarks: Text and abstract disagree on the density uncertainty at the lowest water content (0.8 % vs 0.08 %); 0.08 % is more consistent with the abstract and with the stated agreement within 0.7 % with Joffrion and Eubank. Table 1 row x = 0.1739, 465.95 K, 8.958 MPa lies below that mixture's dew point (Td 467.9 K, pd 9.04 MPa), so it may be in the two-phase region. Table 1 densities are gas-phase (homogeneous vapour/supercritical) mixture densities, not liquid. Authors find Abdulagatov et al. (1993) and Shmonov et al. (1993) data inaccurate.

extraction_notes: Script-parsed from the text layer by splitting each line into the left and right block at a fixed character column; blocks stacked left then right. Headers made ASCII: rho for the Greek letter, 'mol.m-3' for mol·m^-3 (printed mid-dot written as full stop), d for delta. Every cell compared with the 250 dpi page images of journal pp. 449 and 455: no corrections. Sanity: within each x block T and p strictly increase and rho strictly decreases (isochore with vessel expansion). Table 1 property set to rho_gas_loaded with the overall water mole fraction as the composition column 'x' (mapped as columns.x_h2o_mixture, fill_down); Table 2 mapped as y_h2o at the dew point (basis saturation) with the saturated-vapour density as value2.
